title: Constrained Convolutional Neural Networks for Weakly Supervised Segmentation
authors: Deepak Pathak, Philipp Krähenbühl, Trevor Darrell
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
conclusions: Proposes Constrained CNN (CCNN): trains a CNN for weakly-supervised semantic segmentation by imposing arbitrary linear constraints (e.g. suppression, foreground presence, background-area bounds, and optional object-size bounds) on the expected pixel-label distribution instead of on the raw network output.

Key trick: introduces a latent distribution P(X) constrained to the feasible region and trains the network Q to match P via KL divergence, turning a hard non-convex constrained problem into an alternating convex (dual ascent on P) / gradient (SGD on theta) optimization that plugs directly into standard SGD.

The linear constraints bound expected sums of per-pixel label probabilities (i.e. soft counts of pixels predicted with a given label) within [a,b] ranges - a count-style constraint on the predicted labeling, analogous in spirit to a soft/rational relaxation of a hard prediction-count cap.

Solved via projected dual gradient ascent on Lagrange multipliers lambda (a dual/Lagrangian-style update), which the paper shows converges within ~50 iterations and is robust to initialization, unlike prior MIL-based weak segmentation methods.

Empirically achieves state-of-the-art weakly-supervised semantic segmentation on PASCAL VOC 2012 using only image-level tags, with further gains from adding a rough object-size supervision signal; also compared against fully supervised methods and shown to approach their performance with additional weak supervision.

This is a segmentation-specific, per-image linear-constraint framework (not a transductive, dataset-wide hard prediction-count cap with a ratcheting multiplier/optimizer reset/undershoot hinge as in our method).
